families.s: HSE safety in grain, flour milling and animal-feed production
families.t: grain dust, conveyors, mills, silos, engulfment, atmosphere, noise, transport and tipping
f: Grain and feed work involves manual handling, falls, transport, machinery and harmful substances.
Screw conveyors, rotary valves, roller mills and mixers are common machinery hazards.
Silo entry can expose workers to engulfment, unsafe atmospheres and sweep-auger hazards.
Tipping trailers and lift trucks create transport risks.
Grain and flour dust can cause occupational asthma.
Mills, grinders, graders and bagging lines can create damaging noise.
Milling and pneumatic transfer can generate explosible dust clouds.
Extraction, housekeeping, ignition control and explosion relief are core preventive measures.

families.s: HSE injury and flour-dust controls in bakeries
families.t: mixers, moulders, ovens, racks, slips, flour dust, silos, respiratory sensitisation
f: Bakery injuries arise from handling, slips, falls, machinery, transport and hot equipment.
Mixers, dough brakes, moulders, conveyors and wrapping machinery require safeguarding.
Wheeled racks and sacks create pushing, pulling and lifting risks.
Silo entry can involve engulfment, unsafe atmosphere and mechanical hazards.
Flour dust can irritate eyes and nose and cause dermatitis.
Sensitised workers can develop occupational asthma.
Exposure to flour dust should be reduced as far below the exposure limit as reasonably practicable.
Low-dust flour is a substitution measure that can reduce dust during sieving and tipping.

families.s: HSE substitution of low-dust flour to reduce baker's asthma risk
families.t: substitution, sieving, tipping, dusting, dustiness testing, exposure reduction, RPE, cleaning
f: Traditional wheat flour dust is a major cause of baker's asthma.
Employers must reduce flour-dust exposure as low as reasonably practicable.
Low-dust flour can replace normal flour where flour is needed as a release agent.
HSE testing found substantial reductions during manual sieving.
HSE testing also found substantial reductions during tipping and filling tasks.
Lower airborne dust reduces the quantity breathed by workers.
Low-dust flour should be combined with careful handling and other controls.
A food-industry case study reported reduced exposure, less waste and reduced reliance on RPE.

families.s: HSE dairy-processing safety and occupational-health controls
families.t: wet floors, CIP, steam, hot water, tankers, packaging, ammonia, noise and handling
f: Dairy work includes manual handling, wet-floor slips and falling-object hazards.
Cleaning chemicals, steam, hot water and CIP failures can expose workers to burns and harmful substances.
Falls can occur from ladders, stairs, tanks, vehicles and tankers.
Tankers and lift trucks require workplace-transport controls.
Conveyors, lifting equipment and packaging machinery require suitable guarding.
Repetitive packing and wheeled-rack handling can cause musculoskeletal disorders.
Homogenisers, bottling lines, chillers and pneumatics can create damaging noise.
Chlorine, hypochlorite and ammonia exposures require COSHH assessment and source control.

families.s: HSE safety controls in fruit and vegetable processing
families.t: boxes, sacks, wet floors, tools, conveyors, packaging, refrigerants, repetitive sorting
f: Fruit and vegetable processing involves heavy or awkward loads and sharp-edged containers.
Wet floors and obstructions create slip and trip hazards.
Falling packages and hand tools can strike or cut workers.
Conveyors, bagging, form-fill-seal and palletising machines require guarding.
Cleaning chemicals and ammonia refrigerant leaks can create harmful exposures.
Lift trucks are a significant workplace-transport hazard.
Repetitive sorting and packing can cause upper-limb disorders.
Wheeled units should be stable, maintained and loaded so operators retain visibility.
